Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Sidiberlin
Message:
Self-hosted per-user agent runner orchestrator for Open WebUI

Replaces OWUI's Enterprise-licensed "Terminals" orchestrator. OWUI sees one
plain Open Terminal endpoint; this multiplexes an ephemeral, per-user runner
container behind it.

  OWUI backend --K1 + X-User-Id--> orchestrator --derived key--> runner
                                        |
                                   docker-socket-proxy

Components
  runner/        Open Terminal base + pinned openCode (glibc), non-root
  orchestrator/  FastAPI: lifecycle, reconciliation, budget, quota, role
                 mapper, streaming reverse proxy (14 modules)
  tests/         144 tests: 72 unit (no docker) + 72 integration (real stack)

Verified live against OWUI the OWUI host (v0.11.1): config via API, OWUI's
own verify returning {"status":true,"type":"terminal"}, and real user traffic
reaching a per-user runner.

Seven bugs found by running it rather than reading it, all fixed and
regression-tested:

  N10  WorkingDir=/app (root-owned) broke every relative-path write while
       absolute paths worked -- silent and half-broken
  N14  /data as a host bind mount was unwritable by the non-root orchestrator,
       so the quota cache silently reset on every restart
  N18  runners that died out of band held MAX_CONTAINERS slots until
       IDLE_TIMEOUT: three crashes meant a 30-minute total lockout
  N19  the idle sweep could reap a runner between admission and connection,
       handing the user a 502 mid-call
  N21  the memory gate read /proc/meminfo inside a container, which
       Docker-on-LXC virtualises (534 MiB reported vs 1908 actual), so it
       refused users while the host had GBs free
  N25  agent-authored HTML was served as text/html from OWUI's own origin with
       no CSP -- a stored-XSS path to the OWUI session token
  N27  reconcile() matched on the managed label alone, so a second
       orchestrator on the same host adopted the other's runners and reaped
       them under its own IDLE_TIMEOUT. Killed a live session twice.

Design history, including the decisions these findings overturned, is in
docs/DESIGN-HISTORY.md. Accepted (not closed) risks are in the README:
the socket proxy is a speed bump not a wall, apparmor=unconfined on LXC,
one shared runner network, plaintext K1 on the LAN, polled disk quota.

.env is gitignored. tests/env.test is committed deliberately -- its values
are fake and the suite needs them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
